system_overview: A specification of Misra's algorithm for computing the set of nodes reachable from a given root node in a directed graph. The algorithm is a variant of breadth-first search that differs from the standard algorithm in that the set of visited nodes and the frontier set may overlap, making it amenable to parallel implementation. Written in PlusCal with an attached translation.
actors_and_components: A single sequential process that explores the graph. It maintains a set of visited (marked) nodes and a frontier set of nodes yet to be fully explored. The algorithm picks nodes from the frontier and either marks them and adds their successors to the frontier, or removes them if already marked.
state_variables: Three state variables: (1) the set of nodes that have been marked (visited), (2) the frontier set of nodes to explore (which may overlap with marked nodes, unlike standard breadth-first search), and (3) a program counter tracking whether the algorithm is running or has terminated.
initial_state: The marked set is empty. The frontier contains only the root node. The program counter indicates the algorithm is at the start of its main loop.
actions: One main action with two cases, chosen nondeterministically from the frontier. If the chosen node is not yet marked: add it to the marked set and add all its successors to the frontier (without removing the node from the frontier). If the chosen node is already marked: remove it from the frontier. The algorithm terminates when the frontier is empty.
safety_properties: Partial correctness: when the algorithm terminates, the marked set equals exactly the set of nodes reachable from the root. This is established through three invariants: (1) every successor of a marked node is in the marked set or the frontier, (2) the union of the marked set and the nodes reachable from the frontier equals the nodes reachable from the union of marked and frontier, (3) the set of nodes reachable from the root equals the marked set plus nodes reachable from the frontier. A type correctness invariant ensures both sets contain only valid graph nodes.
liveness_properties: If the set of reachable nodes is finite, the algorithm eventually terminates. This follows from weak fairness of the main action: the frontier cannot remain non-empty forever because each cycle of the loop either adds a new element to the finite marked set or removes an element from the frontier.
additional_assumptions: The root is assumed to be a valid node in the graph. The algorithm works correctly for both finite and infinite graphs, but termination is guaranteed only when the reachable set is finite. The key insight of Misra's variant is that allowing overlap between marked and frontier nodes simplifies parallelization, as described in the companion parallel implementation module.
